findings.claim: The mechanism clause cannot fully separate the claimed two-flow mechanism from the simpler story that the OR flag merely anticipates Gold's volatility ahead of the volatility yardsticks, because both sigmas used to standardize are backward-looking. The lag weakness the entry names for the first sigma applies to the second as well at the 10- and 20-day horizons, and the observed standardized ratios sit just above the bar, so even a modest lead effect matters to interpretation.
findings.evidence: Entry §2, 'The confound': 'har_scaled is built from past returns and lags a jump in Gold's vol, so a state that fires at the start of stress spells could clear the ratio on that lag alone. The second σ is Gold's trailing 10-day realized σ, scaled to the horizon, which catches a jump within days.' For a 10- or 20-day forward window that begins at a vol jump, catching it 'within days' still leaves most of the window divided by a pre-jump σ. KB-016 shows the OR flag is built to fire ahead of stress (recall 0.722 vs 0.333 at 5d), so flag-on days plausibly precede rises in Gold's volatility; such a state would clear the 1.15 ratio while remaining, in the entry's own words, 'a vol forecast restated'. Report §'Gold rival check' gives standardized ratios of 1.18–1.29 against the 1.15 bar. Non-blocking because the test the rules require was named, pre-registered and run; the caveat qualifies what a positive sealed read would mean.

brief.case_against: The strongest argument against spending the one sealed read is the entry's own honesty table. On the practice data the two conditioners beat the do-nothing baseline by only a few thousandths of a skill point, with uncertainty bands that include zero, against a promotion bar of two hundredths. Because the interesting days are about one in eleven, an all-days score will very likely miss that bar even if the width pattern is real, so the read probably comes back 'no skill' and teaches little beyond what is already known. The pattern also rests on eleven stressed episodes, seven of them in 2010–2011, so it leans heavily on one crisis era. And the mechanism test cannot fully separate the claimed tug-of-war in Gold from the simpler story that the warning flag merely sees Gold's volatility coming before the volatility yardsticks do. Nothing here breaks a rule: every threshold was written down before the look, every number checks, and the entry itself leaves the spend to the owner. That is the best case against; I found nothing blocking.
brief.what_it_claims: On days when the stock market is at least five percent below its peak and the project's crash-warning flag is on, Gold's moves over the following one, two and four weeks spread out in both directions — bigger gains and bigger losses — roughly a quarter to a half wider than on similar stressed days with the flag off. Most of that extra spread survives after accounting for Gold's own recent volatility, which is the main alternative explanation. The entry claims nothing about which direction Gold goes. It asks for one test on data from 2018 onward that has never been touched, with every threshold fixed in advance and a minimum sample size set, and it promises to publish the result in the Knowledge Base whether it passes or fails.
brief.what_would_change_it: The concerns are disclosed rather than hidden, so only evidence moves them. Two things would strengthen the case before the key is turned: a check that the width split survives when Gold's forward moves are measured against the volatility that actually arrived over the window — which would kill the 'flag merely foresees volatility' explanation — or a sign the split is not carried by the 2010–2011 episodes alone. Otherwise the honest route is the one proposed: run the single sealed read exactly as designed. If it clears the skill bar against both rivals and the width clause under both volatility yardsticks, my concerns are wrong. If it returns a clean structure-only result, that is still a publishable answer; the owner's real decision is whether one irreversible read is a fair price for it.

brief.case_against: The entry set itself a test before looking, loosened it after looking, and now claims it was passed. On 2026-09-25, the day before the data run, the entry promised that Gold's stressed-and-flagged outcome spread would be at least 1.4 times the normal spread at every horizon. The run measured 1.31, 1.39 and 1.52 — short of 1.4 at two of three horizons. The next day the written requirement became 1.2, and the entry now says 'the pre-registered prediction held' and that it was committed before the run. The git record contradicts both statements. Under the test as originally written, the entry fails its own gate for promotion. The project has already ruled, for a sibling entry, that a width prediction adjusted after seeing data must be labelled 'seen', not pre-registered; this entry does not do that. Everything else checks out: every quoted number matches the report, all data are pre-seal, the run is on the ledger, the floor and slice were fixed in advance. A secondary caution: the flagged cell's episodes concentrate in 2010–2011, so the effect may lean on one era.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a real drawdown (down at least five percent from its peak) and the project's stress flag is on, Gold's returns over the following one, two and four weeks spread out in both directions — bigger up-moves and bigger down-moves — without saying which direction. The core claim is that this spreading is larger than Gold's own recent volatility can explain: about thirty to fifty percent wider in raw terms, and still fifteen to twenty-nine percent wider after dividing out volatility, depending on the yardstick. The proposal is to spend the project's single sealed read (2018 onward) testing whether Gold's predicted quartiles, conditioned on this state, beat both a no-information baseline and the project's existing volatility forecast, with the volatility-adjusted spreading as the mechanism check, a minimum cell size fixed in advance, and a written result either way. It is explicitly not a buy or sell signal.
brief.what_would_change_it: An honest record. Rewrite the entry to state that the original 1.4-times test was set before the look and failed at two of three horizons, that the 1.2 threshold was chosen after seeing the data, and that the raw-width prediction is therefore 'seen', not pre-registered — exactly how the project treated the sibling entry H-008. The part fixed before the look that genuinely held is the volatility-adjusted spreading (bar 1.15, measured 1.18–1.29 under both yardsticks), and that is the clause the sealed read would actually enforce, so the underlying proposal survives an honest write-up. The owner can then judge whether a real but modest effect — one the explore data say is far too small to clear the project's skill bar across all dates — is worth the single sealed read. A per-year breakdown showing the widening is not carried by 2010–2011 alone would further steady it.

The dry run this entry rests on ran its data to mid-2019, and its report includes a year-by-year table counting stressed days in 2018 and 2019 — sealed dates. The headline numbers the entry quotes are genuinely pre-2018, but the run was not clean, and the record now describes part of the sealed period's stress pattern before the single sealed read. Second, the bet is weak even if the pattern is real. The two candidate arms showed almost no forecasting skill in exploration — at best about four thousandths where the bar demands two hundredths, with uncertainty spanning zero — and they must also beat the project's existing volatility forecast, which matched the best arm in exploration. The width pattern cleared its own bar only narrowly at one corner. The entry itself calls the prior low. Promotion most likely spends the one irreversible read on a negative.
brief.what_it_claims: On days when the stock market sits five percent or more below its peak and the project's stress flag is on, gold's moves over the next one, two and four weeks spread out in both directions about a third to a half more than on equally stressed days without the flag. Part of that extra spread is just gold's own volatility; roughly a fifth to a third of it is not. The entry claims no direction for gold. It proposes one test of this width pattern on unseen post-2017 data, against the project's existing volatility forecast, and promises to publish the result either way.
brief.what_would_change_it: The rule break is fixable: re-run the exploration with the data ending in 2017 so nothing sealed is tabulated, and show the quoted cells — which already appear to be pre-2018 — are unchanged. That clears the blocking finding without moving any bar, since the prediction and the floor predate the run. The weak-skill concern cannot be argued away with current evidence: the entry would need to justify why candidates that scored near zero in exploration deserve the single sealed read, or the owner accepts spending it on a likely negative. findings.claim: The entry calls itself a two-sided width claim, but the confirm read it actually proposes is a hit rate on the direction of gold's return — a sign with a confidence attached.
findings.evidence: Entry, 'What would test it': 'the confirm read: on stressed, OR-Elevated days, the share of days on which Gold's 20-day forward change is positive, against a coin-flip 50%. A share above 55% on the sealed slice, with a binomial interval clear of 50%, is the bar.' A share-of-positive-days test with an interval clear of 50% is exactly 'a sign with a confidence attached', which the rules (§7) call 'ADR-0009 territory in a new coat, regardless of how the question is phrased'. It also contradicts the entry's own text: the mechanism says 'The flag should say nothing about which way Gold goes', the target-space check asserts 'No location claim. brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a drawdown of at least five percent and a fragility alarm is firing — meaning one of three stress gauges sits in the top tenth of its own history — gold's returns over the following one, two and four weeks spread out in both directions: the middle band of likely outcomes gets wider, by more than gold's own recent volatility can explain. The sealed read itself is protected by the entry's own eight-episode floor, so a spent read would at worst come back 'underpowered'; but the owner should know that, and that the practice-skill numbers point to a likely failure on the confirm bar, before turning the key. If the owner consciously chooses to spend the read as a pre-committed falsification of a two-episode pattern, that is an informed spend — the entry as written does not let them make that choice, because it hides the episode count.

brief.case_against: The entry's log of what was looked at is incomplete, and under the project's rules that alone disqualifies it. The report behind it was committed twice: once on the evening of 25 September — hours after the prediction was written — with different bin edges and a smaller minimum cell size, and once on 26 September with the settings the entry reports. Even with a clean ledger the spend is weak: the effect lives in about one day in eleven, the skill bar is scored over all days, and in rehearsal the arms scored essentially zero on that bar — so the single sealed read would likely fail its headline test even if the width story is true. brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a drawdown of at least five percent and the project's early-warning flag is switched on, gold's moves over the following one to four weeks spread out more in both directions — up and down — than on stressed days when the flag is off, by roughly a third to a half in rehearsal data, and part of that extra spread survives after dividing out gold's own recent volatility. brief.what_would_change_it: First, restore the missing 25 September run to the ledger — its settings and what it showed — or show it tested nothing relevant, then re-audit the corrected text; that is the blocking item. Beyond it: a mechanism test comparing flag-on and flag-off days inside the same stress episode, so a volatility jump at a spell's start cannot fake the effect; and either a skill bar scored on the stressed days rather than all days (written for the class before any candidate, as the rules require) or your explicit acceptance that the headline skill test will probably fail and the width-ratio clause is the real read. A sealed read clearing 1.15 under both volatility measures while beating both comparators would prove the low rehearsal prior wrong.
